This November has been a terrific month for the number six, with GTA 6 approaching and The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel finally out in the open. Once GTA 6 is in our hands at last, we'll have to reckon with a strange new world where we're no longer constantly waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto – the kind of alien sensation that Hollow Knight: Silksong players, who practically grieved yearning after so much buildup, are intimately familiar with.

Will The Elder Scrolls 6 step up to the plate as the next [clears throat] Massive Sequel Over a Decade in the Making That Also Has the Number Six in It? Is it going to fill Rockstar's enormous shoes as gaming's white whale?

"No, I don't think it is," says Circana games analyst Mat Piscatella when I mention this idea in passing. "It's a huge game, obviously, but things like Grand Theft Auto, Call of Duty, NBA 2K, these are games that are huge, mass-market appeal titles."

This reflects part of what makes GTA 6 so interesting, not as a game to be played but as an outlier to be observed. Similar to Nintendo, Rockstar can basically do whatever it wants because its loyal audience is big enough. More uniquely, Grand Theft Auto is the type of game that appeals to a huge range of players, from the enthusiasts playing dozens of the best games of 2026 to casual fans who mostly stick to the sports and shooter series that Piscatella mentions.

"They're their own thing," he says. "It's a different set of rules, a different set of expectations. They're gonna do their thing, and they've earned every bit of that, just based on what they've done. Nintendo is its own thing, too. They are unique, and I know people hate that and go, 'They're competing just like everyone else.' They are, but with the IP and their history and how they've developed how they go to market, it is a unique proposition. That's why they can do things other companies can't, and they have a relationship with their players that other platforms don't. These are companies or developers that are doing their own thing, blazing their own trail, and a lot of other people try to follow."

As AAA game development faces cost crises, Rockstar is making the biggest bet of all, and with the most favorable odds imaginable. Nobody else could make a game like GTA 6. For anyone but Rockstar, it would be too big to succeed. "If you want to talk about a big bet, they don't come any bigger than this, and the appetite for big bets like this doesn't exist in many places," says Piscatella.

Even The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, follow-up to one of the most-played RPGs of all time, and handily the most-modded, is in a different weight class. (The Witcher 3 and Skyrim have both sold 65 million copies.)

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"Whether you're talking about an Elder Scrolls, a Witcher, a God of War, those are big games but they're nowhere near the scale of an NBA 2K, Call of Duty, or Grand Theft Auto," adds Piscatella. "No shade to them. They're all great games and perform very well. But we're talking about a secondary tier to those real mass-market hit drivers."

It certainly doesn't help that The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced eight years ago, and re-announced this week with a subtitle, yet we still don't even have a screenshot. The game is reportedly looking at a 2029 launch, which would put it 18 years post-Skyrim, so I'm going to need Bethesda to wake me up for the third time when, and only when, it's got some heat.

Bethesda wants you to "show off your excitement" for The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel by spending $35 on a T-shirt

#4271. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

#4270. AMD FSR Upscaling 4.1 Has Officially Arrived For Xbox Series X|S

"We can't wait to see what developers create with it."

A couple of weeks ago, the folks at AMD made headlines when they announced that AMD FSR 4.1 would be coming to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S in the near future, and the rollout has officially begun today!

As a result of this, developers will have access to a new method of improving visual fidelity (and in some cases boosting performance) in their games across both consoles, which should prove particularly useful when it comes to the lower-powered Xbox Series S.

"Working closely with AMD, the XBOX team has optimized AMD FSR™ Upscaling 4 for XBOX Series X|S, making ML-based upscaling practical on the consoles' RDNA 2-based GPUs. These optimizations enable developers to benefit from improved image quality while balancing GPU performance, helping them deliver better visual experiences on existing XBOX hardware."

"The new Microsoft GDK sample demonstrates how to integrate FSR4 across XBOX Series X|S and Windows using AMD’s FSR SDK. It includes both Full and Lite INT8 models, allowing developers to explore different rendering resolutions and evaluate the tradeoffs between image quality and performance."

Of course, it's still early days right now and we don't have any real-world examples of AMD FSR 4.1 working on XBOX Series X|S just yet, but we assume developers of all kinds will start integrating it into their games going forward.

Not only should this lead to improved experiences in demanding XBOX Series X|S titles, but it should also mean the two consoles remain capable for many years to come, even after Project Helix arrives in the next generation.

News AMD FSR 4.1 Announced For Xbox Series X|S And ROG Xbox Handhelds

"And there's even more ahead with Project Helix..."

@Banjo- Logically, Rockstar will apply it to GTA VI, because it's a very simple feature to implement.

As for your comparison with QSSR, it is currently only supported by two games on PS5: Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei. At this stage, it is mostly a marketing feature with very little real impact for players. In reality, AMD's QSSR is derived from FSR, but in a much more limited form because, as you mentioned, the base PS5 lacks some native hardware features that are available on the Xbox Series consoles.

Furthermore, it is more complex for third-party developers, as it requires genuine porting work. As a result, this technology will likely remain limited to a small number of PlayStation-exclusive titles.

FSR, on the other hand, is a technology that has been deployed much more broadly by game developers, as it is already widely used on PC.

The case of PlayStation's PSSR, which is only available on the PS5 Pro, is different. The PS5 Pro already includes more native hardware capabilities than the base PS5 and is significantly more powerful. Even then, PSSR is also derived from FSR 4, although it still does not match FSR 4 at equivalent hardware performance levels. PSSR has seen greater adoption among developers, but the numbers remain relatively modest in practice. We're talking about roughly 200 games that support PSSR, which is still a small figure compared to the total number of games released each year.

What is certain is that PlayStation's marketing around GTA VI is misleading, or at the very least requires significant nuance. If we're talking about the base PS5, then the claim is false: GTA VI would run better on Xbox Series consoles with FSR 4.1.2. On PS5 Pro, however, GTA VI would likely perform better, which is hardly surprising given that it is a more powerful mid-generation refresh released later and sold at a significantly higher price. However, its price-to-performance ratio remains relatively poor.

Given the relatively small install base of the PS5 Pro compared to the standard PS5, the Xbox Series remains the most obvious value-for-money choice for the majority of players interested in GTA VI.

The claim that GTA VI or other games runs better on PS5 is simply false, on the contrary.

Connect stars to harvest their energy, extend your fleeting life, and build your score. Shape constellations freely, and take risks with advanced techniques to earn additional energy and points. Faraway’s simple rule-set and flowing controls are easy to approach but demanding to master. Every run begins from nothing, in a universe generated in real time around your performance.

Hasbro Games Junior Collection (Outright Games, 6th Nov, $29.99) - Play Monopoly Jr., Clue Jr., and The Game of Life Jr. Customize your avatar, unlock rewards, and enjoy local multiplayer fun for up to 4 players. Get ready for a big, colorful game night full of laughs, surprises, and “just one more turn!” moments! This collection brings 3 classic junior board games to life in one exciting video game made for kids and families.

Manairons – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition (JanduSoft, 29th Oct, $18.74) - The Manairons are back… and this time, they’re not staying quiet! Manairons is a 3D action platformer game set in the Pyrenees, where ancient legends mix with smoking factories, mischievous magic, and quirky little creatures. You are Nai, a manairó who has just awakened from centuries locked in the ""canut"", a magical artifact as old as it is suspicious. A witch frees you (very timely, indeed) and gives you a mission: recover the ""canut"" and stop the chaos it’s causing. The culprit? Llorenç, a landowner with zero charisma and a lot of machines.

Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition (CDE Entertainment, 5th Nov, $39.99) - Fire up a wild ride across the cosmos with a fresh take on Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy. In this action-adventure game, you are Star-Lord leading the unpredictable Guardians from one explosion of chaos to the next. You got this. Probably. The Encore Edition is exclusive to Nintendo Switch 2 and includes a new set of outfits for Star-Lord, Drax, Gamora, Rocket and Groot. Dressed in 1980s glam rock threads, the Guardians are ready to bring down the house. Literally. - Read our Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition review

Review Marvel's Guardians Of The Galaxy: Encore Edition (Switch 2) - A Bright And Charming Adventure With An Okay Port

Prinny Party: Going Overboard! - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition (NIS America, 11th Nov, $29.99) - Get your friends together for Prinny Party: Going Overboard! In this party game, you’ll traverse the board as you take down demons, earn experience, and buy new equipment—all to make sure you’re strong enough to beat Laharl, the Supreme Overboard!

Shelterra the Skyworld – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition (KEMCO, 5th Nov, $18.89) - Soar into an epic fantasy RPG adventure across Shelterra, a vast floating continent untouched by the mysterious corruption known as Odium. Claude dreams of becoming a professional adventurer, but a simple escort mission soon reveals a threat that could send his entire homeland crashing to the surface. When he discovers that his talking stone is actually an Artifact, a spirit destined to protect Shelterra, Claude joins forces with the Orlok regime and sets out on a journey through the Skyworld to uncover its secrets and save the floating continent from destruction.

Shrek 2 Remastered (Aspyr, 10th Nov, $26.99) - The cult-classic, button-mashing co-op adventure is back with all your favorite characters and improved graphics. Journey through the fairytale kingdom of Far Far Away from Shrek’s swamp to Fiona’s castle and everywhere in between, in a classic action-adventure experience inspired by the DreamWorks Animation movie. Play solo or with up to three friends in co-op, take control of your favorite Shrek heroes as you smash, throw and kick your way against iconic characters from the franchise.

Sword of the Sea (Fictions, 29th Oct, $23.99) - Surf across magnificent waves of sand and glistening waters on an epic quest to restore a lost ocean in Sword of the Sea. From the visionary artist behind ABZÛ, The Pathless, and Journey – Sword of the Sea is an atmospheric surfing adventure with highspeed Hoversword movement inspired by skateboarding and snowboarding.

Excellent. Love the satisfying click of an opening briefcase. Come on in, pal. Here's all the "dirt" we uncovered on this "Titanium Court": So, lotta people have heard of this game, but not a lot are coming clean about what it actually is. Now as for the genre we were having a lot of trouble pinning that down from testimony alone, so we "acquired" a copy to see what was up. (Hey what's a private investigation without a little bit of larceny, right?

Warhammer Survivors (Auroch Digital, 10th Nov, $7.19) - Warhammer Survivors is a fast-paced roguelite survivors' game, pitting a host of iconic Warhammer characters against endless hordes of enemies from multiple Warhammer factions. Developed by Auroch Digital (Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun) in partnership with Warhammer and poncle (Vampire Survivors), discover the universes of Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer: Age of Sigmar in all its pixel glory in this new surviv-a-ton.

ZERO PARADES: Director’s Cut (ZA/UM, 3rd Nov, $35.99) - From the creators of Disco Elysium comes ZERO PARADES - the acclaimed espionage RPG, now expanded with the DIRECTOR'S CUT. You're a brilliant but tormented operant on one final desperate assignment. Prove yourself on the world stage - or blow it all up again. - Read our ZERO PARADES: Director’s Cut review

Review Zero Parades: Director's Cut (Switch 2) - ZA/UM Returns With Another Atmospheric, Cerebral Yet Overly Familiar RPG

A Snail’s Tale (Something Classic, 11th Nov, $12.99) - A retro RPG that asks the age old question: would you take a world of riches in exchange for being chased by an immortal, killer snail? Once upon a time, a commoner was granted his wish to become the king of a vast nation. In exchange, he is constantly chased by an immortal killer snail. Now the king is facing his end of the bargain.

Arcade Archives PREHISTORIC ISLE (HAMSTER, 29th Oct, $7.99) - "PREHISTORIC ISLE" is a shooting game released by SNK in 1989. As the protagonist heads to Greenhell Island to investigate a series of shipwrecks off the coast of the Bahamas, prehistoric dragons thought to have gone extinct launch a relentless attack. The option unit equipped to your aircraft can be repositioned to change its attack method into 5 different types based on its location, such as firing flame lasers upward or dropping bombs diagonally downward. Make full use of your option unit to face various obstacles and uncover the truth behind the mysterious shipwrecks!

Big Jhow Jet (Nerd Games, 7th Nov, $6.99) - Prepare for takeoff! Strap on your homemade jetpack, defy gravity, and unleash total chaos to save your friends from the dreaded Bacon Factory! Jhow is a brilliant, tech-obsessed piglet whose peaceful farm life is shattered when an ominous corporate truck kidnaps all his friends.

Black Lily’s Tale (1000-REKA, 29th Oct, $13.00) - Includes a Nintendo Switch™-exclusive After Story & all DLC scenarios! ―――What is Black Lily's Tale? "Black Lily's Tale", featuring delicate and beautiful art by Fukahire. A unique choice-making systems that will have you seeing visual novel decisions in a whole new light. Pure but not naive, classic but not cliché. A yuri game that will make you strive toward the best ending! You can intervene and lead these girls to happiness.

Castlebound (Ogre Pixel, 11th Nov, $9.99) - Fight hordes of evil monsters and defend your castle in this 1-4 player action platformer with Roguelike elements! Castlebound is a thrilling roguelike action game where you and your allies must defend a walking castle while battling relentless waves of monstrous foes.

Cat-Astrophy (Pdpartid@games, 5th Nov, $14.99) - Cat-Astrophy is a fast-paced, challenging space action roguelite: its Star Cursor system and evolving modules force you to adapt your build and playstyle in every run, generating chaotic combat and precise jumps. The game delivers constant tension and rewards both improvisation and technical mastery.

Don Bradman Cricket JR (Tru Blu Games, 5th Nov, $19.99) - Out of the highly successful Don Bradman simulation series comes Don Bradman JR, the hard-hitting arcade cricket game. Step onto the pitch and feel the thrill of every shot. Don Bradman Cricket JR is fast, accessible cricket that's easy to learn and rewarding to master. Smash boundaries, outplay opponents and make every run count. Pick up and play with intuitive controls. Every delivery is a contest: read the line, time the shot, find the gap. Got five minutes? Play a fast match. Got the afternoon? Play the full cricket experience.

Dungeon Of Dragon Knight Remake (Shanghai QuanYu Network Technology, 5th Nov, $14.99) - Dungeon Of Dragon Knight Remake is a first-person dungeon-crawling RPG inspired by classic role-playing adventures. Create your own party and venture deep into dangerous dungeons filled with monsters, traps, puzzles and hidden secrets. Carefully explore your surroundings, discover concealed passages and mechanisms, collect weapons, armor and useful items, and strengthen your party through battle.

EGGCONSOLE Harry Fox MSX Special MSX (D4 Enterprise, 5th Nov, $6.49) - This title is an adventure game originally released by Microcabin in 1986. While retaining the touching core story—a mother fox setting off toward the distant Reel Shrine in search of fried tofu (abura-age), rumored to be a miracle cure for her terminally ill kit—this unique MSX arranged port drastically overhauls the original gameplay systems. The game has evolved into a deeply engaging, RPG-like experience.

Eternal Palace Sakura (Shochiku, 5th Nov, $11.99) - Eternal Palace Sakura is a fast-paced, exhilarating roguelite 3D action game set in a fantastical Japanese-style dungeon that never stops changing shape. Take control of Retla, a dual-blade-wielding heroine, and face countless trials as you climb toward the top of a beautiful labyrinth where cherry blossoms drift through the air. Enjoy intuitive combo action and strategic build crafting, combining different skills and power-up items on every run.

Faraway (Annapurna Interactive, 5th Nov, $7.99) - Faraway is an endless procedurally generated, mastery-driven arcade game about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive. Connect stars to harvest their energy, extend your fleeting life, and build your score. Shape constellations freely, and take risks with advanced techniques to earn additional energy and points. Faraway’s simple rule-set and flowing controls are easy to approach but demanding to master.

Gemporium (Merge Conflict Studio, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Grow your small gem business in this short, casual simulation miner, Gemporium! Manage your time wisely between mining gemstones, refining them for more profit, and selling them to awaiting customers. After your Grandmole goes on vacation, you’re in charge of running her shop, and you quickly learn it also comes with a price of massive debt. Now, on top of building your business, you must appease the Loan Shark without going broke!

Hasbro Games Junior Collection (Outright Games, 6th Nov, $29.99) - Play Monopoly Jr., Clue Jr., and The Game of Life Jr. Customize your avatar, unlock rewards, and enjoy local multiplayer fun for up to 4 players. Get ready for a big, colorful game night full of laughs, surprises, and “just one more turn!” moments! This collection brings 3 classic junior board games to life in one exciting video game made for kids and families.

Hillthorn (Raw Fury, 10th Nov, $14.99) - Only the foolish and the desperate attempt to wander the mazelike trails of Hillthorn. Even those who know their way may still stumble upon dangerous wildlife or a local villager’s piercing gaze. But a child has gone missing, time is in short supply, and you’re the one being tasked with unraveling the mountain’s secrets. Welcome to Hillthorn, a dark investigation game unlike any other, where the mystery unfolds without a single word spoken.

HorrorVale: Deadluxe Edition (Electric Airship, 31st Oct, $17.99) - Your next-door neighbors are zombies, reanimated monsters deliver the mail and ghosts hide out in your bathroom. Don't worry about anybody you kill along the way–-everyone is already dead! Muahahha! Bash monsters, recruit 30+ friends, and solve brain-buster puzzles! Welcome to the Underworld. . .

Hundred Fires: OPEN VECTOR -Episode 1- (David Amado Fernández, 29th Oct, $6.99) - HUNDRED FIRES: OPEN VECTOR — Episode 1 is a third-person action and stealth adventure set in an alternate Cold War. You play as Merche, a guerrilla and expert thief sent on a mission that quickly turns into something much bigger. Armed with a katana, a pistol and automatic weapons, you'll have to infiltrate secret facilities, deal with enemy soldiers and uncover the secrets behind the mysterious Ancient Weapons. The katana is at the heart of the game. Use it in combat, but also use it to cut through parts of the environment.

Kingdom of Night (DANGEN Entertainment, 5th Nov, $17.99) - Kingdom of Night is an 80s-inspired isometric action RPG where coming-of-age drama meets cosmic horror. When a satanic cult unleashes the ancient evil Baphomet on the small town of Miami, Arizona, high school student John must fight through a night of demonic chaos to rescue his friends before the town is lost forever. Choose from five distinct classes—Barbarian, Knight, Rogue, Necromancer, or Sorcerer—and customize your build with expansive skill trees, powerful loot, and unique equipment.

K-Pop Rising – Dream to Shine (Microids, 5th Nov, $34.99) - Make your dream come true and become a K-Pop Star in this exciting life sim and rhythm game! Together with your best friend Nova, you've always dreamed of making your mark in the world of K-Pop… Now it's time to shine! Throw yourself into the race for fame and let your talent sparkle, from the practice rooms to the stage! Create a group that reflects who you are and, together, set out to conquer the world's biggest stages. Take inspiration from your idols and grow your fan community on social media! Music is your world, and passion is your driving force: you are the future of K-Pop!

LightQb (Restless Corp, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Twenty-three handcrafted levels. One directional dash. And a narrator who will not let a single mistake go unmentioned. LightQb is a fast, unforgiving first-person platformer built entirely around movement. Chain dashes, air control and raw momentum to fly through neon structures, then do it all again a second faster.

Lilac ~side Witch~ (Frontwing, 5th Nov, $24.99) - A fantasy visual novel set in a magic school where humans and mages mingle. Follow Emil, a young human who despises mages, and Henri, a self-proclaimed "bonehead" of a mage, as they learn how to connect in spite of various anxieties and differing backgrounds. Features numerous beautiful characters designed by industry veteran Oyari Ashito! Lilac Academy.

Lilac ~side Wizard~ (Frontwing, 5th Nov, $24.99) - A fantasy visual novel set in a magic school where humans and mages mingle. Follow Emil, a young human who despises mages, and Henri, a self-proclaimed "bonehead" of a mage, as they learn how to connect in spite of various anxieties and differing backgrounds. Features numerous beautiful characters designed by industry veteran Oyari Ashito! Lilac Academy.

Make it! Karaage (SAT-BOX, 5th Nov, $6.99) - Let's make karaage on Nintendo Switch! Marinate the meat in sauce, coat it in batter, and fry it until crispy! Pack up the finished karaage and add toppings to match each order! Share Joy-Con, and up to 4 players can play together! Reach for the ultimate high score! Make karaage to order! Keep cooking until time runs out!

Next of Kin: Epiphany (Spelkvall, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Step into the world of "Next of Kin: Epiphany," where you become private detective Dennis Monroe, a relentless investigator driven to catch the infamous "Epiphany Killer," a shadowy figure who has haunted the city for over twenty years. Every clue draws you closer to the truth, but danger lurks behind every revelation. In the thrilling conclusion to the "Next of Kin" trilogy, you'll explore atmospheric locations, interrogate suspects with the powerful new "Expose" system, and unravel the chilling truth behind the notorious "Epiphany Killer".

Nyghtmare: The Ninth King (Caracal Games, 31st Oct, $4.99) - Centuries after vanishing without a trace, the Kingdom of Mortemire suddenly reappears. Alongside it awakens Aryn, a young woman strangely unaffected by the mysterious call surrounding the kingdom. Armed with only an iron whip, she ventures into its decaying streets in search of answers, facing the creatures and dangers that have taken hold of the land. Nyghtmare: The Ninth King is a dark-fantasy retro "Vania" experience.

Prinny Party: Going Overboard! (NIS America, 11th Nov, $29.99) - Get your friends together for Prinny Party: Going Overboard! In this party game, you’ll traverse the board as you take down demons, earn experience, and buy new equipment—all to make sure you’re strong enough to beat Laharl, the Supreme Overboard!

Shelterra the Skyworld (KEMCO, 5th Nov, $17.99) - Soar into an epic fantasy RPG adventure across Shelterra, a vast floating continent untouched by the mysterious corruption known as Odium. Claude dreams of becoming a professional adventurer, but a simple escort mission soon reveals a threat that could send his entire homeland crashing to the surface.

Shrek 2 Remastered (Aspyr, 10th Nov, $26.99) - Journey through the fairytale kingdom of Far Far Away from Shrek’s swamp to Fiona’s castle and everywhere in between, in a classic action-adventure experience inspired by the DreamWorks Animation movie. Play solo or with up to three friends in co-op, take control of your favorite Shrek heroes as you smash, throw and kick your way against iconic characters from the franchise.

The Slormancer (Plug In Digital, 5th Nov, $24.99) - The Slormancer is an epic 2D Action-RPG Dungeon Crawling game following a band of outcasts on their fight against hordes of enemies led by The Slormancer! Play as a Mighty Knight, a Fierce Huntress or a Mischievous Mage, master hundreds of abilities and ancestral powers, gear up, fight for the reputation of your kind and prove your value to the realm. Experience fast-paced gameplay, loads of shiny loot, tons of collectibles, countless hours of content, and carefully crafted pixel art. You were born with absolutely no skill whatsoever, and yet you find a way to be the last hope of the realm as the enigmatic Slormancer and his incompetent underling try to conquer the world once again. How great. But like your grandfather once told you: "You might not have the talent but you have the will."

The Transference (JanduSoft, 29th Oct, $9.99) - YOUR OWN HOME HAS BECOME AN ESCAPE ROOM. AND YOU'RE NOT ALONE. The Transference is a first-person mystery thriller escape room that combines puzzles, a story of family secrets, and moments of tension where you'll have to hide to survive. WHO LOCKED YOU IN? AND WHY? You wake up in your home and discover that the doors and windows have been boarded up from the inside. Someone has placed strange riddles throughout the rooms and turned your home into a prison. Explore, search for clues, and find a way out while trying to answer one question: who is behind all this? PUT YOUR WITS TO THE TEST

The Trolley Solution (Take IT Studio!, 29th Oct, $9.99) - Philosophers already waste their time and lives thinking about thinking. Why not have fun while doing it? The Trolley Solution is a compilation of minigames based on the famous trolley problem, originally proposed in 1967 by British philosopher Philippa Foot. Put your thinking power to the test in humorous iterations of the problem. Unlock a variety of minigames where you can put your gaming skills to the test. Challenge yourself and learn important and useful philosophical knowledge while expanding your mind! Disclaimer: You might not actually learn anything useful or important, nor expand your mind, by playing this game.

" He's so dejected that he accidentally drops the ring he used to propose into a storm drain. The ring keeps falling deeper and deeper underground. It falls into the sewers, then further down into. . . a movie theater? Wait, is that a jet plane? Why are we in the Old West now? What are cowboys doing underground? ? ?

Unpetrified: Echoes of Nature (Mindscape, 10th Nov, $29.99) - Unpetrified: Echoes of Nature is a peaceful and reflective experience, filled with meaningful collectibles, unique emotion-driven interactions, and environmental puzzles. The orchestral soundtrack emphasizes an intimate storyline of unlikely friendship, loss, and love.

VALKYRIE TUNE：Synthesis of Souls (Good Smile Company, 5th Nov, $24.99) - Story An intertwining, resonant serenade of love, sorrow, and fateful encounters calls forth a reboot for the future. Step into the shoes of Rei, who wakes up in the Domed City of Initium surrounded by women calling him the Messiah. Determined to regain the memories he lost during years of cryosleep, he begins living with the six beautiful members of the TUNED (Tactical Unit for Neutralization and Enhanced Defense)-young women who wield so-called harmonic weapons.

Chivalware, Titanium Court, Sword of the Sea, and Tanuki take my fancy. Plenty for the wishlist when things quieten down post-Ocarina. Nothing big releasing in the next few weeks, right?

None of the above floating your boat? Here's a trio of intriguing old games on sale this week - not necessarily The Best™ or The Highest Scoring™, but Switch games that still deserve your attention, especially when they're discounted.

#4268. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is returning to IMAX 70MM screens... again

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is returning to the big screen... again. It's a re-return, if you will.

Per Deadline, The Odyssey will play on 1,000 screens, including IMAX and IMAX 70mm, in North America starting on December 11. This is three weeks after the nearly three-hour-long movie is set for a home release on premium VOD, 4K and DVD on November 17.

The film, which is no doubt going to sweep the Oscars, hit theaters on July 17, and stayed on premium large format screens until September 30 (including 4DX, because who doesn't want to be hit by waves for at least 60 minutes?). It was given a proper theatrical re-release that began on October 9 and lasted until the 31st. We don't know how long the December run will last.

Based on Homer's epic poem, The Odyssey follows Matt Damon's warrior Odysseus as he embarks on a decade-long journey home after the Trojan War, meeting up with some gods, goddesses, cyclops, and sirens along the way. The star-studded cast also includes Anne Hathaway as Odysseus's wife Penelope, Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Himesh Patel, Charlize Theron, Zendaya, Jon Bernthal, John Leguizamo, and Samantha Morton (yes, the very same from Mike Flanagan's Carrie).

The movie grossed over $1.8 billion at the global box office, making it the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time and Universal's highest-grossing movie to date. It's what Homer would've wanted, honestly.

For more, check out our The Odyssey review, and our deep dives into The Odyssey monsters, The Odyssey poem, and The Odyssey ending explained.

#4266. PS6 Development on Track, Sony Making 'Solid Progress' Towards Next-Gen

Work on the PS6 and the next console generation as a whole is currently "progressing as scheduled" at PlayStation, it's been confirmed.

Speaking alongside the release of Sony's latest quarterly financial results, CFO Lin Tao said the company is on track to deliver its next PlayStation system, and it intends to make "solid progress" towards the next generation within the next fiscal year (via VGC).

The quote from Tao reads: "Looking ahead to the next fiscal year, we aim to continue to enhance user engagement and further strengthen monetisation through the release of strong titles and the expansion of our service. We also intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform."

Tao continued by talking up "investment in the new platform" from the start of the next fiscal year. It has to attach "great importance" to a new console and "make the necessary investments" for it. "We have to support the soundness of our platform and think about how rationally we can invest in that platform. We will announce that at an appropriate time in the future."

A few months ago, Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki claimed the firm hadn't yet decided when the PS6 will come out. Consistent rumours point to a release in the next few years, however, with a potential $1,000+ price point and a handheld device to go with it.

With the prices of components still on the rise — which Sony would need to manufacture PS6 hardware — the potential cost of a next-gen machine looks like it'll be the biggest factor in whether PlayStation fans jump on board or not. When we polled Push Square users, 65% of you said you wouldn't pay four figures for a video game console.

Microsoft will also have a new Xbox to launch in the coming years, currently codenamed Xbox Helix, and that's suggested to cost as much as $1,800, depending on whether it decides to subsidise the box. PS6 is at least rumoured to be cheaper to make than Xbox Helix, so the cost shouldn't get quite that high.

Elsewhere in its financial report, Sony confirmed PS5 sales have reached 97.9 million. With a boost from GTA 6, it should hit the 100 million sales milestone by the end of the next quarter, and become the fourth PlayStation system to do so.

@sanderson72 that financial bull was always being released, but the media wasn’t reporting it.

It’s not aimed at customers but investors and such calls have always occurred.

Due to insatiable demand from gamers for any scrap of info, and the games media looking for clicks, these investor calls are now published and picked apart by the media for any juicy snippets. Often the media blow innocuous statements out of proportion and read imaginary conclusions between the lines to create a good story.

In the old days you’d read about this stuff in Edge Magazine, but not your tabloid gaming mags. That persisted into the internet era but over the last Gen or two it’s started to be more prominently reported on the mass consumption consumer websites as opposed to just industry sites.

#4265. Watch the Battlefield 6 Season 2 gameplay reveal here

As promised, our first look at the next Battlefield 6 and Redsec season is nearly upon us.

After a one-month delay, we’re finally days away now from the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 of live service. The second season is being revealed today, following weeks of teasers, and some Battlefield Labs testing of the first new map arriving with the new season.

It’s all going to kick off with a gameplay reveal, which is set to stream live later today.

As we’ve come to expect, the Season 2 reveal will take place via a YouTube premiere. It’s set to kick off live at 8am PT, 11am ET, 4pm GMT on the official Battlefield channel on YouTube - and embedded below. Today’s reveal will also be followed by a more detailed roadmap of Season 2, which will give us a much better idea about the volume and cadence of content we can expect.

Season 2 goes live February 17, kicking off a new chapter in the continued conflict between NATO and Pax Armata. The medium-large new map, Contaminated, will be available immediately at the season’s launch. Contaminated takes placed in the mountains of Germany, centered around a once NATO-owned airbase.

VL-7 psychoactive smoke appears to factor majorly into the gameplay of this new season, though we’re waiting to hear more details on that. We can expect new weapons, new gadgets, and the awaited return of the AH-6 Little Bird helicopter.

Look forward to more coverage from us as more details are revealed later today.

The archival process "preserved an estimated 2500 hours of historical footage"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

EA has just released seven new remasters across Steam and GOG, bringing classics like Wing Commander and Road Rash back to life in greater fidelity than ever before. These remasters were made possible by pure happenstance, when a random EA employee stumbled on an archive of tens of thousands of classic game assets sitting in a storage room.

Producer Jim Vessella had helped shepherd Command & Conquer Remastered to life which, among other things, involved restoring a host of Betacam tapes containing the game's original cutscenes. Those tapes then sat untouched throughout the pandemic, but when Vessella returned to the office in 2022, he suddenly had to figure out where to put all these tapes.

"When I came back from the pandemic in spring of 2022," Vessella tells The Game Business, "I had this giant shelf in my cubicle of 200 Betacam tapes, and I was like, 'I need a place to store this.' One of the facilities people were like, 'oh yeah, I think there's a room over in the other building that has a couple items like that.' So he took me over there, and then you open it up and it's like Indiana Jones. Just woah."

As Vessella explains in a blog breaking down the restoration process in detail, this was "a giant storage room containing nearly 20,000 archival media assets including Betacam, VHS, and D1 tapes among other media like Film Reels, CD-ROMs, and more." He soon started spending his off hours unpacking these boxes, working with other EA employees to organize it and begin the arduous process of digitizing it all.

"The fun began in early 2024." Vessella says. "We hired a small contracting team, purchased 4 Betacam players plus a VCR, and over the next eight weeks we were feeding tapes into the machines on swing shifts for roughly 17 hours every day. I catalogued and drove another 500 tapes of rarer formats (D1, D2, Umatic, and Film Reels) off-site to get digitized by a professional vendor in San Francisco."

By the time it was all done, the team "had digitized a combined 6000 media assets and preserved an estimated 2500 hours of historical footage." That included the master source tapes for Road Rash and much of the Wing Commander franchise. Vessella started reaching out to members of the Wing Commander community to work together on what would become a series of remasters.

One of those modders was Matt Wells, who had already created an Enhancement Patch for Wing Commander 3. Communicating over Slack, Vesella explains, "the cycle became that Matt would release a new build, let us know, and I would playtest that build to pass along feedback, technical notes, and suggestions. In between, we would troubleshoot items over Slack and brainstorm further design ideas. I remember one Saturday night in 2025, we spent hours trying to hunt down a crash, replaying the same mission dozens of times under different parameters and reviewing the log files. I think we got that one, but if you happen to run into a crash, please understand it wasn’t due to lack of trying."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

As modders worked "volunteer hours in the spirit of bringing joy to the greater community," EA also partnered with GOG to work on restoring Wing Commander Prophecy, which didn't have the same level of existing community support. "GOG spent months combining all the elements together, constantly fixing weird little issues, and made significant improvements of their own, adding features like improved controller support and even a gorgeous launcher for configuration setup," Vessella says.

Wing Commander 1, 2, 3, 4, Prophecy, and Privateer 2 have all gotten Anniversary Edition remasters as part of this initiative, which are available on both Steam and GOG. But for my money, Road Rash is the most impressive part of this whole endeavor. Unlike the Wing Commander games, Road Rash had never previously been released on digital platforms, and on top of the remastering work, EA also had a legal nightmare to unpack.

Road Rash – specifically, the 1994 game originally released for 3DO – features an extensive licensed soundtrack, including Soundgarden, Paw, Hammerbox, Monster Magnet, Therapy?, and Swervedriver. In order to make this re-release happen, EA would have to go and relicense all that old music.

"Successfully pulling this off would require connecting with the music label and every band member who controlled a 'side' of the 14 tracks. By the summer of 2026, we had agreements in place with 6 of the 7 bands (including the most prominent band on the list), but after months of searching we still could not find one of the members for a specific band," Vessella explains.

"No contact equals no license. So by September 2026, we were days away from needing to pull the rip cord and begin extracting the band’s music from the 30th Anniversary Edition. And then like out of a Hollywood movie, we tried one more lead which was somehow able to put us in touch. We turned around the final license in mid-Sept, allowing us to celebrate the full legacy of Road Rash, breathing a sign of relief in the process."

"There is no game preservation with DRM": Why GOG's leaders have spent 18 years fighting for classic games

He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.
